title: React Security Applied Check
description: Apply React security knowledge to tricky XSS, CSRF, auth-storage, dependency, rendering, and secret-handling scenarios.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A profile page renders user bio HTML from an API with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. What is required before doing this?

options.text: Trust the source or sanitize the HTML with a proven sanitizer

questions.explanation: Raw HTML rendering must be controlled carefully; naming or memoization does not make untrusted HTML safe.

questions.prompt: A user-controlled URL is placed in an anchor href without validation. Which risk should you consider?

options.text: Unsafe schemes such as `javascript:` or phishing redirects
React will stop escaping all text

questions.explanation: User-controlled URLs need scheme and destination validation because escaping text is not enough for URL safety.

questions.prompt: A cookie-authenticated API accepts `POST /transfer` with no CSRF token or SameSite protection. What is the concern?

options.text: Another site may trigger an authenticated state-changing request
Source maps will leak bundle size

questions.explanation: CSRF protections matter for cookie-authenticated state-changing operations.

questions.prompt: A developer says CORS is enough CSRF protection. What is the correction?

options.text: CORS is not a substitute for CSRF defenses on cookie-authenticated writes

questions.explanation: CORS and CSRF solve different problems; CSRF needs safe methods, SameSite, tokens, or similar defenses.

questions.prompt: An access token is stored in localStorage and the app later has an XSS bug. What is the main added risk?

options.text: The token can be read by injected JavaScript

questions.explanation: localStorage is accessible to JavaScript, so XSS can expose tokens stored there.

questions.prompt: Before adding a new UI dependency, what should you review? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Whether it asks for secrets in client config

questions.explanation: Dependency security includes trust, maintenance, audit findings, bundle awareness, and suspicious setup requirements.

questions.prompt: A `.env.production` file with private keys is committed and referenced by a React build. What should happen?

options.text: Rotate exposed secrets and move private operations to a trusted backend
Rename the file and keep using the same keys
Add the keys to VITE_ variables
Rely on minification to hide them

questions.explanation: Committed or bundled secrets should be considered exposed and rotated; client builds cannot keep them private.

questions.prompt: A protected route briefly renders private content before auth loading finishes. What is the safer UI pattern?

options.text: Render an explicit loading or unknown-auth state until access is known
Fetch private data before checking auth

questions.explanation: Protected routes need loading states that avoid flashing private UI while authentication is unresolved.
